name: Cryptic crossword No 28,032
preamble: Twelve solutions have something in common, not further defined

clue.text: Boatman catches a crab — strangely shocking

indicators.note: something done strangely is done in an odd, unusual way, so these letters come out in an unusual order
to catch something is to grab it and hold it, so one piece closes around another

blocks.note: Boatman is the setter, so the setter's name means 'me'
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The setter, out rowing, fumbles a stroke and 'catches a crab', which is a weirdly alarming moment.
explanation.walkthrough: To catch a crab is a rowing term for a botched stroke, so the surface feels nautical. A setter's pseudonym in the clue usually stands for ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Something macabre is gruesome or ghastly, dwelling on death, so it is fittingly called shocking.

clue.text: Baffled by sensational wordplay with nine letters missing

indicators.note: whatever is missing has been taken away, so part of the word is removed
to play with something is to toy with it and mix it about, so the order is jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
the four letters that spell the number nine, which are the ones removed

explanation.surface: Someone is bewildered by a dazzling pun that leaves out a whole run of letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nine letters' does not mean nine letters are dropped: it means the letters N, I, N, E. Strip them from the long word and seven letters are left to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at a loss means not knowing what to do or think, which is exactly what being baffled or puzzled is.

clue.text: Initially, Alexander's charming

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: the opening letter of the name
cute means attractive in an endearing, charming way

explanation.surface: A remark that, from the very start, Alexander is a charmer.
explanation.walkthrough: One of twelve theme answers that each go before TRIANGLE, so the clue is wordplay only: an acute triangle.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclued theme entry: an acute triangle has all three of its internal angles smaller than ninety degrees.

clue.text: Lower part of rigging cut from triangle, part of a ladder

indicators.note: in a down entry the lower part of a word is its bottom, that is its final letter
what is cut from something is removed from it, so a letter is taken out

blocks.note: the final letter of the word
taken as written; the remaining seven letters are then rearranged

explanation.surface: Sailing talk: a bit is trimmed off the lower rigging, a triangle of rope, to make part of a ladder.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no word signalling the rearrangement: the seven letters left after the cut must simply be reordered. 'Lower part of rigging' looks like a definition, since ratlines are rigging, but it supplies one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratlines are the small ropes tied across a ship's shrouds to form rungs that sailors climb, a rope ladder up the mast.

clue.text: Saucy postcard, not right to publish to online audience

indicators.note: 'not' tells you to leave something out, so a letter is removed
saucy means cheeky and impudent, behaving out of order, so these letters are put out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the standard abbreviation for right, the letter dropped

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a cheeky seaside postcard is not proper material to share with people online.
explanation.walkthrough: Saucy postcards, with rude jokes and cartoons, are a British seaside tradition. Remove the R and rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To podcast is to release audio episodes over the internet, so it is a verb meaning to broadcast to listeners on the web.

clue.text: Love, dropping its first subtle shimmering

indicators.note: to drop something is to let it fall away, so the opening letter of that word is taken out of the other
a shimmering image wavers and shifts, so these letters shift into a new order

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O; the word's first letter, L, is what is dropped
taken as written, losing the L

explanation.surface: A romance, losing its first glow, has become a subtle shimmer.
explanation.walkthrough: Theme answer, defined only by TRIANGLE: an obtuse triangle. 'Love' does double work: it gives O, and its first letter L is the one removed from the other word.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclued theme entry: an obtuse triangle has one internal angle wider than ninety degrees.

clue.text: Trick to snort some drug in

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside it, so a letter goes into the middle of a word

blocks.note: a con is a swindle or trick
a snort and a grunt are both piggy noises
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A dodge for sniffing a bit of a narcotic inside somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Theme answer before TRIANGLE: congruent triangles. 'Snort' suggests taking drugs, but it is just a noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclued theme entry: congruent triangles are identical in size and shape, matching side for side.

clue.text: Get to the top on Tyneside?

blocks.note: to scale a peak is to climb to its summit
Tyneside, around Newcastle, is in the North East of England, abbreviated NE

explanation.surface: A question about reaching the summit in the Newcastle area.
explanation.walkthrough: Theme answer before TRIANGLE. In a down entry 'on' means placed above, so the climbing word sits on top of the region.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclued theme entry: a scalene triangle has three sides all of different lengths.

clue.text: Evergreen version of pea, encased in pot

indicators.note: a new version is a reworked form, so these letters are reworked into another order
being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece is held within another

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a jar is a pot or container

explanation.surface: Gardening: a pea variety, sealed up in a pot, stays green all year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Encased' reads like the container signal, but it belongs in the letters to be rearranged; the signal for holding is 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese cedar, or sugi, is a conifer that keeps its needles all year, so it is an evergreen tree.

clue.text: Sauce from the heart of Czechoslovakia's capital

indicators.note: the heart is the centre, so only the middle letters are kept and the ends are dropped

blocks.note: the capital was Prague; its middle four letters are kept

explanation.surface: A sauce said to come from the centre of Prague.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital is not written in the clue: name it first, then trim off its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragù is an Italian meat sauce, most famously the slow-cooked Bolognese served with pasta.

clue.text: First to try lead part with singers in audition: they get a good reception

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, so only that letter is used
an audition is a hearing, so the words are to be judged by how they are heard

blocks.note: the opening letter
the van, short for vanguard, is the leading part of an army or procession
tenors are male singers; in a non-rhotic British accent the word sounds like this ending

explanation.surface: Advice for an audition: go for the lead role first, among the singers, and you'll be well received.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone works only in accents that drop the final R, as most British speech does. 'Reception' here is signal reception, not applause.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerials on a set pick up broadcast signals; good reception is their whole job, a pun on a warm welcome.

clue.text: Cyclisme à vélo?

indicators.note: French for cycling: letters go round like a wheel, so the front ones move to the back

blocks.note: vélo is French for bike; its opening two letters move to the end

explanation.walkthrough: Theme answer before TRIANGLE: a love triangle. 'Cyclisme à vélo' is French for cycling by bike; the word for bike is cycled round, its first two letters going to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclued theme entry: a love triangle is a romance involving three people, two of them rivals.

clue.text: Motley beast or bad boy once

blocks.note: a donkey, a beast of burden
taken as written
a Teddy boy or Ted was a 1950s British youth in Edwardian dress, seen as a delinquent

explanation.surface: Describing a scruffy, multicoloured creature, or a former tearaway.
explanation.walkthrough: Teds, or Teddy boys, were 1950s British youths in drape jackets and drainpipe trousers, feared as troublemakers.
explanation.definitionFit: A motley collection is a varied mixture of things, which is what an assorted collection also is.

clue.text: Pole loses ice, melting first

indicators.note: melting things lose their shape and flow into new forms, so the letters reform in another order

blocks.note: S for south, one of the two poles
taken as written

explanation.surface: A polar region sheds its ice cover, the melting coming first.
explanation.walkthrough: Theme answer before TRIANGLE. 'Pole' looks like a whole word for the letter mix, but it is just S; the Polish reading is a decoy too.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclued theme entry: an isosceles triangle has two sides of equal length and two equal base angles.

clue.text: Initially sleepy, got up, then tea: in winter you may need more than one of these

definitions.text: winter you may need more than one of these

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is taken
in a down entry going up means reading from the bottom, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: the opening letter
to have won something is to have got it
cha, or char, is British slang for tea
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drowsy morning: get up, have a cuppa, and in winter you will need a few more of these.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' works twice: it ends the wordplay and opens the definition. Cha is old British slang for a cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Snow chains are fitted to car tyres for grip on icy roads, and are needed in sets, one per driven wheel.

clue.text: Cleaner to hearten lady? Quite the opposite

blocks.note: the opposite of hearten: to discourage someone
the opposite of a lady is a gentleman

explanation.surface: A charwoman wonders whether to cheer up a lady, or rather the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quite the opposite' tells you to swap each word for its antonym rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Detergent is a cleansing agent such as washing powder or washing-up liquid, so it is a cleaner.

clue.text: Boatman — to relish, ultimately, or detest

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the word is used

blocks.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman, a sailor
the final letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: The setter himself asks whether he enjoys something or hates it.
explanation.walkthrough: Boatman is the setter's name, which suggests ME as at 1 across, but here it means a sailor: an AB.
explanation.definitionFit: To abhor something is to regard it with disgust and hatred, a stronger synonym for detest.

clue.text: Permit one to move after damaging allegations

indicators.note: moving means leaving one's place, so a letter quits its spot and is put back later on

blocks.note: to bear something is to tolerate or permit it
mud is smears and damaging accusations, as in mudslinging
a means one, as in 'a dog'

explanation.surface: Someone is allowed to relocate after a scandal of harmful accusations.
explanation.walkthrough: Theme answer before TRIANGLE: the Bermuda Triangle. The A inside the word for permit leaves its place and goes after the word for smears.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclued theme entry: the Bermuda Triangle is an area of the Atlantic famed for ships and planes vanishing.

clue.text: 'Cheap digs', opined resentful Spooner

indicators.note: Dr Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so the initial sounds are exchanged

blocks.note: opined means said and resentful means bitter; swap their opening sounds

explanation.surface: A sour Dr Spooner grumbles about his cheap lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: A bedsitter, or bedsit, is British for a single rented room used for both living and sleeping. 'Digs' is British slang for lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedsit is a small one-room rental, the cheapest sort of lodgings, so fits cheap digs.

clue.text: Two left arms waving?

indicators.note: something waving moves back and forth, so these letters are shaken into another order

blocks.note: two in Roman numerals
L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written

explanation.surface: A clumsy person with two left arms flails them about.
explanation.walkthrough: Theme answer before TRIANGLE: similar triangles. The surface plays on 'two left feet'.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclued theme entry: similar triangles share the same angles and shape, differing only in size.

clue.text: Set the trend, able to ignore the odds

indicators.note: the odd positions are first, third, fifth and so on; skipping those keeps the even ones

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on

explanation.surface: A trendsetter able to defy the odds.
explanation.walkthrough: Theme answer before TRIANGLE: the eternal triangle. 'Ignore the odds' sounds like beating long odds, but means skipping letters in odd positions.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclued theme entry: the eternal triangle is the age-old dramatic situation of two lovers and a rival.

clue.text: Little information about vintage

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information, short for general information
vintage means old, of an earlier era

explanation.surface: Scant details are known about a wine's vintage.
explanation.walkthrough: Theme answer before TRIANGLE: the Golden Triangle, the opium-growing region where Thailand, Laos and Myanmar meet.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclued theme entry: the Golden Triangle is the border area of Thailand, Laos and Myanmar known for opium.

clue.text: Cruets of liquid sugar

indicators.note: a liquid flows freely and takes any shape, so these letters flow into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Table containers full of runny sweetener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of' is part of the letters to rearrange, not a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Fructose is the simple sugar found in fruit and honey, one of the main sugars in the diet.

clue.text: Herbs: bases for sauces, say

indicators.note: 'say' means as spoken, so the word is judged by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: a roux is cooked flour and butter, the base for many sauces; the plural is said 'rooz'

explanation.surface: A note that herbs are the foundation of sauces.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural of the sauce base is spelt the same as the singular but pronounced with a z sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Rue is a bitter-leaved aromatic shrub once used in medicine and cooking, so rues are herbs.

clue.text: Change of direction in match

indicators.note: changing direction means turning one way instead of the other, so one direction letter is swapped for its counterpart

blocks.note: a match is a light, as in 'got a light?'; its L for left becomes R

explanation.surface: Turning the other way in the middle of a football game.
explanation.walkthrough: Theme answer before TRIANGLE: a right triangle, or right-angled triangle. Left becomes right.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclued theme entry: a right triangle has one angle of exactly ninety degrees.

clue.text: Game animal, endangered (about the last in Punjab) in organised slaughter

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, so only that one is taken
about means around, so one piece wraps around another
being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: a cull is the planned killing of animals
the giant panda is a famous endangered animal
the final letter

explanation.surface: A hunted animal at risk, with a Punjab link, caught up in a planned slaughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game animal' reads as one phrase meaning quarry, but 'Game' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cup-and-ball is a traditional toy game in which a ball on a string is flicked up and caught in a cup.

clue.text: See 16
Rising at first, but getting smaller overall

indicators.note: at first means at the start, so only the opening letter is used
over all means covering everything, so one piece goes over and around the other

blocks.note: waning means shrinking, like the moon after full
the opening letter

explanation.surface: Something that goes up at the start but ends up shrinking, like a deflating soufflé.
explanation.walkthrough: Theme answer before TRIANGLE: the red warning triangle placed behind a broken-down car. 'Rising' and 'smaller' look like opposites to balance, but supply letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclued theme entry: a warning triangle is the reflective sign set on the road behind a stopped vehicle.

clue.text: UK citizen stands by Labour leader boxed in by Trotskyite extremes, likely to snap

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the opening letter is used
extremes are the far ends, so only the outermost letters are kept
something boxed in is enclosed on all sides, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: a Brit is a British person
the first and last letters
the opening letter

explanation.surface: A Briton stays loyal to the Labour Party leader, hemmed in by hard-left Trotskyites, and is close to breaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stands by' sounds like loyalty but only places one piece next to the next.
explanation.definitionFit: Something brittle is hard but fragile and breaks easily, so it is likely to snap.
